This small plot of 0.09 hectares is for my yam and cassava, which my family depends on for food. I own the land so I take care of it well, but money is tight and fertilizer is expensive — I will put a little NPK on the yam mounds and add manure from my goats to stretch it. I save my own yam setts and cassava cuttings from last year like my father did, and I do not irrigate because we depend on the rains here in the middle belt. Most of the work — making mounds, planting, weeding, and harvesting — I do myself with my wife and older children, and I will only hire a few hands for the heavy mound-making at the start.
